relations: As the submerged wedge rotates from steep to horizontal, it descends through the amber layer toward the interface.
The wedge's downward settling drags the reddish-orange interface band lower and flattens its curved boundary.
Internal motion from the settling wedge reconfigures the suspended specks and bubbles in the upper amber layer.
The glass rim, outline, and gray backdrop remain fixed while the contents slowly settle.
caption: The video showcases a clear tapered glass tumbler resting on a dark reflective surface against a smooth gray gradient backdrop. Inside, two stratified liquids fill the vessel, a dark brown lower layer and a translucent amber upper layer, divided by a reddish-orange interface band. A bright orange wedge is submerged, pressed against the right inner wall of the glass. Fine suspended specks and small bubbles drift gently throughout the upper amber layer. Over the course of the clip the wedge gradually shifts downward and rotates, moving from a steeply angled position toward a flatter, more horizontal orientation lower in the glass. The reddish-orange interface band slowly descends and flattens as the wedge settles, while the specks reconfigure with the internal motion. The glass outline, rim, and background remain fixed, indicating a static camera observing the slow settling of the contents.
